text:
C
haotic power churns inside of you. Bards of the
College of Chaos harness the wild forces of
chaos and creation, allowing them to perform
powerful and unpredictable feats.
Yours is not a formal bardic college. Bards of
Chaos are most usually expelled from other
schools after setting fire to the stage or calling
down accidental lightning strikes. Your performances are
wild affairs, and both your music and your magic can shred
the air with chaotic power.
Maybe your abilities originated after been exposed to the
plane of chaos, or maybe you simply developed a penchant for
raising hell. Whatever the reason, you can unleash raw,
destructive power - making you a terrible threat to both
enemies and allies alike.
label: class_description

text:
Bards of the College of Chivalry champion the values of
honour and justice, acting as knightly protectors to the
common folk during their travels. Though some do travel
from town to town like other bards, a few of this college can
be found in the ranks of armies as knights and officers.
label: class_description

text:
Members of the College of Fear learn all the secrets of the
True Fear, and know how to frighten others by telling horror
stories or exploiting their worst phobias. It is said that gazing
directly at the eyes of one of them is enough to cause you
nightmares for the rest of your life...
label: class_description

text:
Inspiring stories and heroic tales are aplenty, but it is a bard’s
skill in regaling such fantastical tales that make them truly
come alive and rouse audiences to action. The bards of the
College of Heroes go about from tavern to tavern, spreading
these exhilarating fables to empower and inspire the masses.
Some even have the privilege of having an audience with a
royal court to put on such performances, or perhaps help
weave their own royal tale of heroism.
Storytelling isn’t the only skill of the bards of this college.
So finely attuned they are to the lore and legends of heroes
past, they can summon their essence to aid them. Creativity
is best taken from its source, and who better to talk to than
the actual heroes of old?
label: class_description

text:
Bards of the College of Liturgies, also known as Cantors,
embrace religion and piety. They devote themselves to the
teachings of a higher power and often become pilgrims, using
their magical voices to spread the dogma of their faith in
hopes of changing the world for the best. Their psalms are
empowered by divine magic, harmonious to the ears of the
devout and excruciating to those of little faith and vile hearts.
label: class_description

text:
Bards of the College of Reflections consider themselves as
the centrepiece for all their tales and performances. They will
accept nothing less than a reputation akin to godhood where
people will revere them wherever they go. Bards of other
colleges consider this college to be filled with narcissistic and
vain people, though they still can’t deny the level of
showmanship and competency they have when it comes to
entertaining others.
label: class_description

text:
he College of Flavour is home to bards who use the taste to inspire the world.Whether a baker, chef, or saucier,a bard that walks the path of flavour is an 

Such bards are a great asset to many-a-party, for there are few things more certain than an adventurer's hunger.There are many reasons one may be drawn to adventuring.They may be searching for a secret mythical ingredient,wish to complete a world class recipe book, or to explore the wonders other cultures have to offer.
label: class_description

text: Bards who join the College of Fools use crude stories, daring acrobatics, and cutting jokes to entertain audiences, ranging from tavern crowds to royal courts. Where other Bards seek out forgotten lore or tales of bravery, Fools tell embarrassing and hilarious stories of all kinds. Fools undermine the plans of the powerful, and their acrobatic ability to tumble, dodge,leap, and climb makes them slippery opponents in battle.
label: class_description

text:
ou are one of the few and proud inducted into.the prestigious College of Metal, founded by Sabbath The Black. A strange breed of Bards,.the members of this college are known for their.love of loud music and raucous, near-violent parties which often involve a strange form of. dance-combat; a style copied by their more 

enthusiastic fans. They wade ecstatically into war, being able to strike hard against their foes or empower their allies with their music. The flames of the Abyss in their tongues, the horns of Valhalla in their songs, the spirit of demons and the  undead in their hearts; they are like roiling thunder crashing through the battlefield with booming voice and cacophonous performance.
label: class_description

text:
Bards of the College of Puppetry are master manipulators,individuals who revel in the subtlety of their art. While other bards might enjoy the applause of their audiences or the  respect of their peers, these puppeteers enjoy being the guiding hand, the shadow behind the curtain.

Bards of this college gather like others, but typically only to hold grand competitions or induct new members into their illustrious numbers. Each bard will play a performance,.hoping to establish themselves as a master puppeteer. Joint performances are not unheard of, but they are rare, a result of their solitary mindsets.
label: class_description

text:
Worship takes on many forms across the multiverse; the quiet  zealot, and the impassioned preacher spreading the tenants  of their faith across the land with word and song.

Bards of the College of Radiance are devout preachers of the divine, and all their performances sing the praise of their will of their god and inspire devotion in their followers.
label: class_description

text: Bards that join the College  of Revelry somehow seem to be the center of attention wherever  they go. They enjoy the afterparty more than their performance, and they never turn down an invitation to a good time. From formal banquets to harvest celebrations of small towns, Revelry Bards live for the party.
label: class_description

text: Bards of the College of the Voice ridicule paltry singers and tellers of tawdry tales. To them, their voice is their instrument, and the ancient words they speak their performance. Bards of this college are regarded with reverence, for those with the power to join it speak their will into reality. The hills shake with their bellowed incantations,which warp the world to suit their whims. When these bards speak, even the mightiest creatures fall before their words.
label: class_description

text: Some Bards are so  inspired by the majesty of nature they can. draw musical magic. from nature itself... Often more at home.in nature than on the stage, Bards who join the College of the.Wilds feel a special kinship with wild plants and animals of. all kinds. They can use their enchanting music to soothe even the most savage beasts, turning them from enemy to ally..
label: class_description

text:
Adherents of the College of the Wind learn to listen the
melodies of the air and the subtle notes carried by the breeze.
Their life is a duet with the nature, that let them move both
allies and enemies at their will, like feathers in the wind.
label: class_description

text: Most rogues can hide. but few hide in plain sight. From mere disguises to physical changes in color, Chameleons master covert skills both mundane and magical to immerse  themselves into any situation and strike at a moment's notice..
label: class_description

text:
Some rogues find meaning in their lives through prayer and
dedication to a divine ideal. Be it rogues that wish to absolve
themselves of a shady past, or scoundrels discovering a
greater cause, such people harness their talents as enforcers
of various churches, becoming the shadowy hand that erases
enemies of their faith.
label: class_description

text:
Divine Avengers are agents sent by the gods to track and
eliminate the unholy. Some of those rogues are virtuous,
worshiping good gods and bringing their righteous justice to
the world, but some others are darker and follow the twisted
whispers of evil gods, executing their targets in their name.
label: class_description

text: Professional killers and talented socialites, Infiltrators combine a keen eye and quick tongue with mastery of the blade. Glamorous assassins who blend in a variety of societies and situations, their skills are just as sharp and deadly as their knives..
label: class_description

text:
You are an Influencer, a duplicitous manipulator that excels in
using flattery and natural charisma to sway others to your
side. When in a spot of trouble, you can rely on the followers
you’ve garnered to get you out.
label: class_description

text:
In the depths of the underworld, there are all variety of
criminal and unsavory elements. But here and there, you
find one individual so utterly crazed that even the most
hardened criminal is unnerved by their presence. For their
brutality, unpredictability, eccentricity, or some combination
of the three, these mad dogs of the underworld are masters
of the art of keeping their foes on their toes, and then
demonstrating that being on their toes doesn’t matter if their
leg’s been cut open when they weren’t looking, or taken a
club to the head when they fall to the ground.
label: class_description

text:
These non-magical tricksters delight in bamboozling
their dim-witted opponents and pride themselves on
how many times an actual spellcaster has tried and
failed to counterspell them.
label: class_description

text:
The Marauder is a brutish rogue that looks out only for itself.
Such a rogue will not hesitate use innocents as collateral to
protect themselves if need be. For this rogue, concepts such
as pride, honour, and fairness mean nothing in the heat of
combat. The only thing that does matter is who is left alive at
the end of it all.
label: class_description

text:
ou hone your skills in the art of ranged combat,whenever there's a fight you can easily act as  support and help your allies by picking off enemies from a distance. Able to act as using distance and precision as weapons to accomplish your goals and making sure overwatch and executioner, many assassins,

bounty hunters, and spies follow this archetype, able to control the battle from afar and potentially eliminating the target before anyone has a chance to notice you.
label: class_description

text:
The Chocolatier is a whimsical wizard that masters different
schools of magic all for the sake of creating delicious
chocolate. The Chocolatier possesses different magic items
that allow them to mass produce chocolate.
label: class_description

text:
Cooking Prodigy
Cooking Prodigy
2nd-level Chocolatier Magic feature
You are an academic in both the ways of magic and making
chocolate. You gain proficiency in cook’s utensils, and your
proficiency bonus is doubled for any checks made using this
item.
label: feature

text:
The need for wizards in any aspiring army has 
always been a given. But more recently, generals have 
sought more well-rounded wizards that can hold their 
own in the midst of battle. Simply casting strong spells 
from afar is not enough for a wizard. They must also be able
to fight and survive on the front lines with their fellow
soldiers when the need arises.
Wizards of the Combat Magic tradition seek to solve this
problem. They excel at fighting in the fray of battle, getting 
up close and personal with their enemies and quickly
dispatching them using magic.
label: class_description

text:
Fleshwarping is the magical art of altering flesh and
bone. Despite its rather unsavory reputation,
fleshwarping has been practiced by a small number of
wizards who seek to unlock the secrets of flesh.
In Yvarra, fleshwarping first came about during the
Second Arcane Renaissance. Followers of fleshwarping
believe that flesh is the fifth element, consisting of
blood for vitality, bones for purpose, breath for spirit,
and meat for strength.
These wizards are called fleshwarpers. They study
anatomy and wield spells that alter flesh. Many engage
in extreme body modification and medical practices.
label: class_description

text: There are few schools as risky or as dangerous as that of demonology. To study demons, devils and their ilk in an.attempt to learn their secrets and obtain their service is to play with wildfire. Yet, the rewards can be great.
label: class_description

text:
D
eep within hidden dungeons, wizards of the
School of Forbidden Magic push the boundary
of magic into unknown eldritch depths.
Traditional wizarding schools may shun their
practices, yet wizards of Forbidden Magic delve
deep into the dark arts. Yours is the magic of
heresy; you can sacrifice your own flesh and
blood to fuel your spells, and desecrate the souls of the
deceased to harvest their magic.
Wizards of this school are branded as cultists or apostates.
The powers that you learn come with a steep price, but with
them you become capable of both great and terrible feats.
label: class_description

text: The Arcane Tradition of the Gunmage emphasizes the use of a firearm as a spellcasting focus, teaching to release spells in ways which boost the caster's destructive capability. Given that firearms are a recent technological development, the Gun Magic School is still a budding one; though its popularity is rapidly growing due to the effectiveness and appeal of its concepts.
label: class_description

text: From witches to hexmages, the school of hex magic has gained an unsavoury reputation among both scholarly and regular folk alike. It is regarded as a cruel and twisting style of the arcane, manipulating the very fabric of magic to inflict debilitating conditions and restrictions on others. However those who have taken the time to research this field have realised that the school of hex magic is more than just maledictions, as it reaches into every school of magic through rituals and other incantations.
label: class_description

text:
Few monsters are as emblematic to dungeon delving as the  mimic. As fluid shapeshifters, capable of replicating any object or fixture, these curious predators have made themselves a bane to adventurers everywhere. Innumerable histories trace the origin of this age-old monstrosity to a lesser-known wizard, mad tyrant, or sorcerer-king, who constructed the creature from vile magics long ago..

Such tales have led many spellcasters throughout the realms to cultivate a morbid fascination for mimics and their ecology, attempting to emulate the original witchcraft through mad experimentation with shapechanging beings.

After fully delving into occult magic, wizards of this.deranged tradition have developed rituals to transform their own spellbooks into unprecedented hybrids, which are able to feed off the surrounding mana. The holder of such a macabre creation means to harness the power of mimics in its purest form,by tuning the species'anatomy to suit their own crazy blend of sorcery.
label: class_description

text: lerics and paladins have blind faith in their gods.Warlocks and sorcerers gain their abilities because greater wills decide so. You don't have the time or patience to rely on others. As a.School of Mythos wizard, you know there is a.bigger and older power that you can reach and are willing to pay the price of studying and mastering it.
label: class_description

text: izards who are familiar with dunamancy.magic know of its power to bend reality,altering time and gravity to their will. But its properties may go further, and arcane. practitioners of the conjuration school are  some of the ones trying to adapt dunamantic influence to their knowledge. Realiturgy studies the  properties of dunamancy and the ability to use them to shape and empower regular conjuration spells: adapt space around  matter, travel across the universe in a second, or conjure your own reality from a different timeline.
label: class_description

text:
The legends talk about a secret school of wizards that
mastered the powers of the true invisibility... but no one has
ever seen one of them …
label: class_description

text:
In the annals of time, an ancient order of sages known as the
Silver Mages emerges, a venerable lineage of scholars and
mystics who sought to bridge the gap between mortals and
the divine. Venerating the gods with unyielding reverence,
they devoted themselves to unraveling the sacred mysteries
that lie beyond the veil of mortal understanding. From the
hallowed halls of their sanctuaries, these theologians delve
deep into the arcane tapestry of religious knowledge,
becoming masters of divine lore.
label: class_description

text:
These wizards specialise in manipulating and
pilfering the magics of other spellcasters, stealing
their power and making it their own.
label: class_description

text: Wizards of this tradition focus on magic that allows them to achieve very specific goals; primarily reconnaissance, theft,and sabotage. They use powerful illusions to hide their machinations, as well as Divination magic that lets them gather information unseen and unheard. They make  excellent spymasters, working either for themselves or as court wizards for a higher authority that needs their services. Some wizards even use their talents against others of their  kind, weaving webs of intrigue that afford them opportunities to steal others' arcane discoveries.
label: class_description

text:
Many gods claim arcane magic as their domain, due to its
nature. Magic is a living, breathing being, as much a part of
the world as any other primordial force. Just as there are
deities of the hunt, the sun and war, the arcane is a domain
under the jurisdiction of many divine patrons.
Many such divine beings grant their blessings to clerics of
their faith, but often also bid their followers to study wizardry
and arcane spellcraft. Such a dedicated user of magic might
find themselves following the arcane tradition of Theurgy.
label: class_description

text:
Out of all wizards, those most studious and dedicated to
understanding the Art are called universalists. The path many
accomplished archmages chose to walk even as young
practitioners, universalists have no care for perfection of a
single school of magic or casting style, since they believe in
the one True Magic. In pursuing it, they attain incredible
mastery of the arcane, being able to reshape magic in ways
even their colleagues find extraordinary.
To be a universalist, however, is not only about producing
grandiose displays of magical crafting. Universalists, in their
core, understand the Weave, the mana, and some say are
those closest to peering through the veil of magic itself. While
all wizards seek revelations hidden behind the arcane
mystery, universalists see magic as the means of perfecting
themselves and the world around them.
label: class_description

SUGAR AND SPICE

label: feature

When a creature within 60 feet that can hear you makes an attack.roll,you can use your reaction  to expend a Bardic Inspiration die and force it  to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save,the creature must use the  same attack against another creature of your choice within the range of its attack.
label: feature

text: Your nefarious dealings with the lower planes have granted you access to c  dark magics. When you learn a new Bard spell  you can choose the spell from the Bard or the Warlock spell list. It then becomes a Bard spell for you.
label: feature

text:
You can draw upon the dark arts to regenerate your magic,.much as a Warlock does. When you finish a short rest, you.can regain one expended Bard spell slot of a level equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1st-level) or lower.

However, if you choose to use this feature during a short.rest then you cannot use Song of Rest..
label: feature

text:
Your bardic magic is infused with the power of the lower.planes. When a creature under the effect of Countercharm succeeds on a saving throw to resist being charmed or frightened, you can use a reaction to  expend a use of Bardic Inspiration and force a creature  of your choice within range of your Countercharm to  make a Wisdom saving throw.

On a failed save, it is charmed  or frightened (your choice)for the duration of Countercharm.The  creature can repeat its saving at the  end of each turn, and each time it takes damage,ending the charm or frighten effect on a success..
label: feature

text: the Bard spell restores hit  points, one target of the spell additional hit points  equal to your Charisma modifier of 1).All targets  of the spell have advantage on the next attack roll,ability check, or saving throw they make.
label: feature

text: You use your talent for the dramatic to inspire your allies in combat. When a friendly creature that can see or hear you within 30 feet fails an ability check or saving throw, or misses with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, roll it, and the result to the creature's roll, possibly turning its failure into a success.
label: feature

text: The sound of your music inspires great deeds. Creatures of your choice that can hear you within range of Countercharm  gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of their turns.
label: feature

text:
14th-level  College of Drama feature 

The  Muse grants you the ability to enthrall Death itself, if only y for a short while. Your Masks grant the benefits below:

## MAsk Of COmedy 

You can bring allies back from the brink of death. When a creature you can see within 30 feet makes a death saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend a use of Bardic Inspiration and make a Charisma (Performance) check. The creature can choose to use the result of your check in place of making a normal death saving throw roll.

## MAsK OF TrAgedyE 

You can bargain with death itself for more time. When you are reduced to O hit points but not killed outright, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration die to immediately make a Charisma (Performance) check. If the result of your check is a 20 or greater, you fall to 1 hit point instead of 0.
label: feature

text: You wield the melancholic magic of negative emotions and can use it to inflict minor curses. When a creature that can hear you within 60 feet, makes an attack roll, ability check,or saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend a use.of Bardic Inspiration to impose disadvantage on its roll.
label: feature

text:
You have steeped yourself in strange magic and ancient lore.associated with death. Whenever you make an Intelligence check to recall knowledge pertaining to rituals or lore related to death, the undead, or the magic of necromancy, you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll..

Also, whenever you learn a new Bard spell, you can choose.to learn a necromancy spell of your choice from any spell list..
label: feature

text:
You can conjure and bind J  Restless Spirits that died with unfinished business.At the end  of each long rest, you can perform a short ritual that summons  such a Spirit. It is friendly to  both you and your  allies, obeys your 

commands,and uses the  Restless Spirit stat block, which uses your Spell Save DC,, and proficiency bonus (PB).

In combat,the Spirit acts  during your turn. It can move and i  use its reaction on i  its own, but the only action it takes.is the Dodge  action, unless you used your bonus action to.command  it to take one of the actions in  its stat block, or another action. If you are incapacitated,.the  Restless Spirit can take any action  it chooses.
label: feature

text:
You have mastered the use of visual art forms for your bardic magic. You gain proficiency with calligrapher's and painter's supplies, and whenever you make an ability check with either tool you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.

Moreover, you can use calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies as a spellcasting focus for any Bard spell you know.

Finally, whenever you learn a Bard spell, you can choose to learn an illusion spell of your choice from any spell list.
label: feature

text:
Your s  signature bardic magic can bring your artwork to life.You  learn the  find familiar spell, but it doesn't count against your total 1 number of Spells Known. Though, you can only cast  find familiar using calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies as your spellcasting focus.



When you cast find familiar in this way, your familiar resembles a living two-dimensional piece of artwork. As an action, your familiar can flatten itself against any surface to appear as mundane.e art or graffiti. If a creature succeeds on.an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Spell Save DC it realizes that the artwork is a living familiar.
label: feature

text: If you cast an illusion spell and use calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies as your spellcasting focus you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast the spell with a spell slot one level lower than you normally would (minimum of 1st-level).
label: feature

text:
Also from 3rd level, after a creature rolls one of your Bardic Inspiration die, they may regain hit points equal to the roll.In addition, at the start of a creature's turn, they may spend your Bardic Inspiration die to reroll any saving throw they failed since the start of their last turn (no action required).

A creature can benefit from this feature a number of times equal to their proficiency bonus per long rest.
label: feature

text:
Also from 6th level,after a friendly creature you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points, you may administer an invigorating meal as a reaction.The creature rolls a number of their hit dice equal to or less than their proficiency bonus, and regains hit points equal to the total.

A creature can benefit from this feature no more than once per long rest.
label: feature

text:
Your training allows you to move about in strange and bizarrely entertaining ways. You can take the Dash action as a bonus action. When you take the Dash action, you gain the following benefits, which last until the end of your turn:

. Opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage..You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.. You can reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to your Bard level + your Charisma modifier
label: feature

text: You are immune to the frightened condition, and whenever you make a death saving throw you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, roll it. and add the result to your roll.
label: feature

text:
You take up the mantle of a legendary hero, transforming to match the legend. You can use a bonus action to transform into your Heroic Form, gaining the following benefits:

.You gain temporary hit points equal to your Bard level.

.You can take the Dash action as a bonus action so long as you end your movement closer to a hostile creature.

As a reaction when a creature targets you with a melee attack, you can make one attack against that creature.

These benefits last for 1 minute and end early if you fall unconscious or die. Once you use this feature you must finish.a short or long rest before you can transform again..
label: feature

text: You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your Bard cantrips in place of one of those attacks.
label: feature

text: You have trained to overcome any obstacle that may stand in the path of your legend. You gain proficiency in Athletics and.have advantage on saving throws to resist being frightened.
label: feature

text:
Your bond with the ancient hero has enhanced the flavour of
your stories. Your Bardic Inspiration gains certain benefits
depending on the hero summoned.
Healer. When you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die,
it gains temporary hit points equal to the maximum number
of the die. In addition, when the die is used, the creature
regains hit points equal to the number rolled.
Mage. When a creature rolls a Bardic Inspiration die to
add to their ability check or saving throw, it can roll twice and
use the higher number.
Warrior. When a creature rolls a Bardic Inspiration die to
add to their attack roll and hits, it can add the same number
to its damage roll.
label: feature

text:
You learn the thaumaturgy cantrip, which doesn’t count
against the number of bard cantrips you know.
In addition, you learn to speak, read and write Celestial,
and you gain proficiency with the Religion skill.
label: feature

text:
At 3rd level, when a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw,you may use your reaction and expend one of your Bardic Inspiration die to let out a high-pitched scream of pure metal power! One hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your Charisma modifier +your Bardic Inspiration die roll) or be frightened.

Additionally, each creature within 15 feet of you who fails their roll take thunder damage equal to your Bardic Inspiration die roll. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier until you take a long rest.
label: feature

text: At 6th level, you know the Thunderclap cantrip as well as the Thunderwave and Shatter spells. These do not count towards  your spells known. Additionally, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points or score a critical hit, you can cast Thunderclap, Thunderwave or Shatter as a bonus action. You must still spend a spell slot as normal.
label: feature

text: Starting at 14h level, you can unleash a performance the likes.of which few have experienced. As an action, you and all creatures of your choice within 100 feet of you that can hear  gain an inspiration die. These dice are not taken from your Bardic Inspiration pool. Additionally, hostile creatures within  50 feet of you that can hear must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they suffer 8d8 thunder damage and are stunned. On a successful save,they take half as much damage and are not stunned.
label: feature

text:
Also at 3rd level, you choose one style of combat that exploits attraction and desire. Regardless of style, you can use the weapons required to use your feature as a spellcasting focus..

Cupid. You gain proficiency in greatbows, longbows, and recurve bows. When you damage a creature with one of those weapons (or a shortbow), you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC.
label: feature

text: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the College of Puppetry Spells table.Each of these spells counts as a bard spell for you, but doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know.
label: feature

text: Your skill with puppetry transcends the physical. You can add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make that  involve puppets, and you learn the stroke of lunacyOES cantrip. If you already know it, you instead learn one bard cantrip of your choice.
label: feature

text:
When a creature fails its saving throw against one of your bard spells or features, you learn its surface thoughts as if by the detect thoughts spell until the end of your next turn.Additionally, as an action, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be convinced one of the following is true (your choice each time you use this feature):

 Someone just called out to it, using its name if it has one. You choose the general intent of the message,and the sound originates from a location of your choice within 30 feet of the creature, even behind an object or structure.
label: feature

text: When you use your Bardic Inspiration feature, you can puppeteer a creature to your or its benefit. text:
Starting at 2nd level, when you make a Stealth check, you can
add your intelligence modifier to your roll.
label: feature

text:
Beginning at 6th level, when a spell that makes you invisible
should end for you because you have made an attack or you
have casted a spell, you can make an Intelligence saving
throw (DC 15). On a success, the spell doesn't end for you
and you remain invisible.
In addition, when a spell that makes you invisible reaches the
end of its duration, or when you lose you concentration on it,
you remain invisible until the start of your next turn.
label: feature

text:
At 10th level, your ability to cast Hemomancy spells is greatly 
augmented. When you spend hitpoints to cast a spell with the 
hemomancy tag, you now gain temporary hit points equal to the 
total amount spent on the spell.
label: feature

text:
Starting at 6th level, when you damage a creature that is below 
half their hit point maximum with a spell, that creature takes 
additional necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier if 
they haven’t already taken damage from this feature this turn.
label: feature

text:
Also at 2nd level, you gain the ability to create a Divine Space,
a small pocket dimension that reflects your connection to the
divine. As an action, you can create an extradimensional
space that lasts for 1 hour times your Wizard level. The door
to the space appears in an unoccupied space of your choosing
within 30 feet of you.
This space is a 10-foot cube and initially contains only bare
essentials, such as a simple altar, candles, and some religious
symbols. You can dismiss the Divine Space as a bonus action.
While in your Divine Space, you have advantage on
concentration saving throws.
This space expands as you grow, the Divine Space expands in
increments of 5 feet in all directions times your Wizard level.
label: feature

text:
At 6th level, you gain a deeper control over your Divine
Space. You can now add additional features to your Divine
Space when you summon it choosing from one of the
following options:
Healing Font. A small pool of water with healing
properties appears. Once per long rest, you or any
creature within the Divine Space can use a bonus action
to drink from the font and regain hit points equal to your
wizard level.
Knowledge Archive. A bookshelf filled with divine and
theological tomes appears. Over the course of 10 minutes,
you study these books and gain proficiency in one skill or
language of your choice. This benefit lasts until you finish
your next long rest.
Nature's Embrace. The Divine Space transforms into a
tranquil glade filled with natural wonders. You and
friendly creatures within the Divine Space gain the
benefits of the speak with animals spell, and you have
advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks.
Hall of Judgment. The Divine Space shifts into a solemn
courtroom, symbolizing your role as an arbiter of divine
justice. You gain the ability to cast the zone of truth spell
without expending a spell slot, and you have advantage on
Wisdom (Insight) checks.
label: feature

text:
Starting at 2nd level when you choose this
school, you gain an Arcane Vault, a tiny object
which you can use as an arcane focus.
You can use this Vault to dispel and seal
spells.
As an action touch a creature, object, or
magical effect caused by a spell and make an
Intelligence check, DC 10 + the spell's level.
On a successful check, the spell ends on the
target and is sealed in your Vault.
You have disadvantage on the check if the
spell is to high a level for you to cast.
The Vault can seal one spell at a time and can
be emptied with your Stolen Power feature or
during a short rest where you can turn the
power into a temporary hit die that
disappears if not used by the end of
the short rest.
label: feature

text:
Beginning at 6th level, your Vault may now
hold 2 spells.
If the Vault holds two spells you may use an
action to Launder them, turning them back
into raw magic which restores a spell slot of
one type lower than the lowest level spell
sealed in the Vault, minimum 1st level.
You can use this feature a number of times
equal to 1 + your Intelligence modifier. When
you finish a long rest, you regain all expended
uses.
label: feature

text:
At 2nd level, you may use a spell slot of the
same level or higher than the spell sealed in
the Vault to cast it even if it is not a wizard
spell.
label: feature
